title: Normalized canonical CE quotient sequence versus truncation
statement: Let A,B,C be Grothendieck abelian with derived categories, and F:A to B and G:B to C additive left exact. For any family L of second filtrations on mapped CE totals [def-sp-cartan-eilenberg-presentation], the fixed normalized canonical quotient-image model [lem-sp-filtered-complex-canonical-model] has objectwise spectral-sequence isomorphisms to the truncation spectral sequences of the Grothendieck spectral objects. Their canonical page-two comparisons to the interval cohomology objects are natural for every presentation comparison and every filtered lift of its specified total map. No arbitrary external sequence functor E is present, and only page-two naturality is asserted.

source.document: Stacks Project, Homological Algebra and Derived Categories
source.place: Tag 015X, Remark 13.26.15 (second filtration and filtered injective resolution); Tag 015K, Remark 13.21.4 (naturality); Tag 012K (cycle/boundary page construction).

proof.text: Apply the generic normalized decalage comparison to each mapped CE filtered total, obtaining a family a of canonical quotient sequence isomorphisms to decalage-tower sequences. Its first-page square is natural for every filtered map.
Apply the natural CE decalage spectral-object comparison, obtaining b from each concrete decalage spectral object to the Grothendieck derived-truncation spectral object.

Apply exists_pageTwo_functor to the identity functor on abelian spectral objects. Mapping each b through that functor and conjugating by its object comparisons gives a sequence isomorphism c whose page-two comparison is exactly the component of b. Compose e=a followed by c. The generic filtered-map square followed by the cohomology component of the naturality of b gives the required square by associativity. All assembly and normalization steps are complete Lean proofs.

proof_origin.note: G4: decompose through an actual decalage mapping-cone spectral object, separating the universal page comparison from the CE derived-tower comparison. Normalized composition is proved in Lean.

theorem cartanEilenberg_canonical_truncation_comparison
    {A : Type uA} [Category.{vA} A] [Abelian A] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{vA} A]
    {B : Type uB} [Category.{vB} B] [Abelian B] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{vB} B]
    {C : Type uC} [Category.{vC} C] [Abelian C] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{vC} C]
    [HasDerivedCategory A] [HasDerivedCategory B] [HasDerivedCategory C]
    (F : A ⥤ B) (G : B ⥤ C) [F.Additive] [G.Additive]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits F] [PreservesFiniteLimits G]
    (L : ∀ P : CartanEilenbergPresentation F, DecreasingFiltration (P.total G))
    (hL : ∀ (P : CartanEilenbergPresentation F) (p n : ℤ),
      (L P).complexStep p n =
        ((((CartanEilenbergPresentation.mappedFunctor G).obj P.I).secondFiltration n).step p)) :
    ∃ e : ∀ P : CartanEilenbergPresentation F,
      (filteredComplexCanonicalModel C).S.obj
          (⟨P.total G, L P⟩ : FilteredObject (CochainComplex C ℤ)) ≅
        (F.grothendieckSpectralObject G P.X).E₂SpectralSequence,
      ∀ (P Q : CartanEilenbergPresentation F) (d : P.Comparison Q)
        (t : (⟨P.total G, L P⟩ : FilteredObject (CochainComplex C ℤ)) ⟶
          (⟨Q.total G, L Q⟩ : FilteredObject (CochainComplex C ℤ))),
        t.hom = HomologicalComplex₂.total.map
          ((CartanEilenbergPresentation.mappedFunctor G).map d.α) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) →
        ∀ p q : ℤ,
          (((filteredComplexCanonicalModel C).S.map t).hom 2).f (p, q) ≫
              (Abelian.SpectralObject.pageTwoComparison
                (F.grothendieckSpectralObject G Q.X) (e Q) p q (p + q) rfl).hom =
            (Abelian.SpectralObject.pageTwoComparison
              (F.grothendieckSpectralObject G P.X) (e P) p q (p + q) rfl).hom ≫
              (((F.grothendieckSpectralObjectFunctor G).map d.f).hom (p + q)).app
                (ComposableArrows.mk₁
                  (homOfLE (by simp : (q : EInt) ≤ ((q + 1 : ℤ) : EInt))))
